chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Ibn Abi Umayr from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about shortening the prayer (qasr). He said, and he said: 'It is permitted within two farsakhs or the span of a day.'

key_terms.بَيَاضِ يَوْمٍ: The span of a day (duration of daylight/travel)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific distance for shortening prayers during travel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific threshold for the legal status of a traveler (*musafir*) eligible for *qasr* prayer, defining it as two farsakhs or the distance covered in a day. This definition is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for determining when the obligation to shorten prayers begins, distinguishing it from the full four-rak'ah prayer required within the city limits. The reliance on 'a day's travel' reflects the practical application of the *farsakh* measurement in early Islamic geography.
